lessons: ROOT CAUSE worth remembering: the wrong '21-90 day' tik-nisuin window passed every gate for multiple cycles because it HAD a real evidence entry, sourced to nbn.org.il (Nefesh B'Nefesh), a secondary site. The gate checks that a snippet exists at the cited URL, not that the URL is the authoritative issuer. For any rule owned by a ministry, cite the ministry.

PROCESS FAILURE, recorded so it is not repeated: this cycle logged five Expert CRITICALs into lessons[] and pushed anyway. A CRITICAL must block the push or be moved to domain-checklist.md 'Out of scope (explicit)' with a written rationale. lessons[] is for MAJOR/MINOR and for discretionary edits dropped over the Phase 4.1 cap. All five were resolved in v1.5.0.

Expert MAJOR deferred: venue contract commercial terms still uncovered (guaranteed minimum headcount, over-order percentage, vendor and photographer meals charged at plate price, index linkage and any cap on it). The Troubleshooting row already names index linkage as a cause while the skill never teaches the couple to negotiate it, which is the wrong way round. Highest-value MAJOR for the next cycle.

Expert MAJOR deferred: yeduim batzibur and Brit HaZugiut are missing from the non-Rabbanut routes. The skill names exactly the couples who cannot use the Rabbanut and then offers them only the two routes that cost money and a flight. references/legal-and-contract-risks.md already cites procedure 5.2.0009 as the unmarried-partner status track without saying what that status is. Treat as a scope bug, not a nicety.

Expert MAJOR deferred: noise limits and event end-times. Prevention of Nuisances Law 1961 and the Unreasonable Noise Regulations 1990, plus municipal licence conditions, decide when the music legally stops. This is the exposure specific to the garden venues the skill repeatedly recommends for value.

Expert MAJOR deferred: hadrachat kallot certificate is absent from SKILL.md, SKILL_HE.md and references/rabbinate-checklist.md. Many councils gate the file or the mesader kiddushin on it and the courses have limited scheduling. The domain checklist calls it 'partially covered', which overstates the position.

Expert MAJOR deferred: ACUM is stated as a flat legal mandate. What the Copyright Act 2007 creates is a public-performance right; ACUM licenses the authors' and composers' repertoire and T008 is the market settlement of it, not a statutory fee. Performers' and producers' rights are administered separately and can produce a second invoice. Verify before rewriting, then correct the framing.

Expert MAJOR deferred: tax invoice from every vendor. Cash-without-invoice is common in this industry and it destroys the paper trail the skill's own contract advice depends on. One row in the vendor red-flags table would close it.
Expert MAJOR deferred: venue accessibility duty under the Equal Rights for Persons with Disabilities Law 1998, which matters at 200-400 guests and is the venue's duty rather than a favour.
Expert MAJOR deferred: marriage-leave entitlement under collective agreements and IDF/public-sector service conditions. Unclaimed entitlement, costs nothing, administrative window passes.

Expert MAJOR partially addressed: occupancy cap. The wording now points the couple at the figure recorded in the fire approval and licence file, and at the municipal licensing department if the hall will not produce it. The instrument that fixes the figure is still unverified; the Expert points at the planning-and-building permit regime's assembly-places provisions. Verify that before citing it.
Expert MINOR deferred: 'the Rabbinate-approved mesader kiddushin is free' overstates it. No council charge, but a customary payment to the rav is near-universal and couples budget for it.

Expert MINOR deferred: the Kohen restriction list omits a chalutza and a chalala. One clause fixes it and it stays on the right side of the personal-status boundary because it names categories rather than ruling on anyone.
Expert MINOR deferred: the teudat ravakut row says the bureau may take witness testimony instead but never says what the witnesses must be, so a couple can lose an appointment slot fetching them.

Tooling: verify_legal.py's v1.4.0 REVIEW on 'שימו לב לניסוח' did not recur after the rewording to 'נוסח החוק'. scan_catalog.py still reports level 3 on two documented false-positive families (a 'עורך דין' hit where the text refers the user TO a lawyer, and a 'תצהיר' hit where the text explains that item 7.9 has NO declaration route). Neither warrants a detection-set change; a regression fixture for the refer-to-a-lawyer pattern would still be worth adding.

METHOD: two assertions in this cycle's brief did not survive the sources, and both were wrong in the confident direction. The brief said the get-refusal prenup is 'unavailable once married'; Tzohar and ITIM both say it can be signed afterwards, and the pre-chuppah advantage belongs to the property agreement alone. The prior cycle's own note said event/hosting cancellation 'runs on its own timetable under the 2010 regulations'; in fact those regulations INCLUDE Israeli event services at item (8) and the real point is that the reg 2(3) window has closed long before any wedding is cancelled. Verify the brief, not just the skill.

METHOD: the Expert's Sefirat HaOmer CRITICAL was substantively right and its citation was not. It attributed the two minhagim to Rema OC 493:3 as a rule about WEDDINGS; 493:3 is about haircuts, and the wedding rule sits in 493:1. The skill now says exactly that, with the haircut caveat stated in the text. A reviewer finding a real gap is not the same as a reviewer citing it correctly.
